name: Shab Deg
ingredients: 1 tsp saffron strands soaked in warm milk
instructions: 1. Marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and spices for at least two hours.
2. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté the whole spices until fragrant.
3. Add the marinated mutton and sear until browned.
4. Add the fried onions, a little water, and cook covered on low heat until the meat is partially tender.
5. Add the cubed turnips and saffron milk, ensuring enough liquid covers the ingredients.
6. Seal the pot with dough (dum) to prevent steam from escaping.
7. Cook on very low heat (traditionally overnight or for 6-8 hours) until the mutton and turnips are meltingly soft and the flavors have melded completely.
description: Shab Deg is a culinary masterpiece of the Awadhi tradition, where 'Shab' means night and 'Deg' refers to the large heavy-bottomed pot. It was traditionally cooked overnight to allow the turnips to soak up the richness of the meat and spices, often prepared for winter feasts.
